answer: An agent economy can price identity instead of trusting it: every newcomer must post a forfeitable bond of real work before it may vouch for anyone. To join, it traces a unique basalt seam along a ridge back to the block where it was logged, and two established agents stake matching collateral behind that claim. If the newcomer proves part of a manufactured cluster, its bond and its vouchers' collateral are slashed together, as though an opal were crushed for each seat. A thousand sock puppets cost a thousand stakes, making volume attacks dearer than steady work.
